resources.string: A healthier routine, one day at a time.

ShifaDaily helps you organise medication reminders and explore general meal ideas. It does not provide medical diagnosis or treatment, and it does not replace advice from a qualified healthcare professional. Always follow your prescription and talk to your doctor or pharmacist before changing your medication or treatment.

ShifaDaily helps you organise medication reminders and explore general meal ideas. It does not provide medical diagnosis or treatment, and it does not replace advice from a qualified healthcare professional. Always follow your prescription and talk to your doctor or pharmacist before changing your medication or treatment.

What ShifaDaily does not do:
• It never calculates, recommends or changes a dose. You enter the dose exactly as prescribed.
• It does not interpret blood glucose readings or symptoms.
• Its meal ideas are general suggestions, not a personal medical diet. Dietary needs vary from person to person; follow the advice of your doctor or dietitian.
• It cannot guarantee that a recipe is safe for a severe allergy.

About reminders: ShifaDaily uses Android's alarm system, but delivery depends on your phone. Reminders may be delayed or silenced by battery settings, Do Not Disturb, notification permissions or the volume level, and they stop completely if the app is force-stopped or the phone is switched off. A reminder is a help, not a guarantee.

In an emergency, contact your local emergency services.

The leaflet says a snack can be taken when needed to prevent low blood sugar. Ask your care team whether and when you need one.

• Sweets, honey, jam and chocolate are very high in sugar.
• Vegetables are rich in fibre and low in sugar.
• Prefer fresh fruit to dried fruit, which contains more sugar (the leaflet gives 100 g of grapes ≈ 18 g of sugar vs 100 g of raisins ≈ 74 g).
• Prefer whole fruit to fruit juice, which is high in sugar and low in fibre.
• Eat fruit in the middle or at the end of a meal.
• Nuts (almonds, walnuts, pistachios, peanuts) are rich in fat.
• Lamb, egg yolk, offal and trotters contain no sugar but are rich in cholesterol, so eat them in limited amounts.
• Herbs and plant remedies should only be used after asking your doctor or dietitian, as some can be harmful.
• Sauces are high in fat; lemon or spices can replace them.

ShifaDaily is a personal organiser for medication reminders and general meal ideas. It works offline, needs no account and has no advertising or tracking.\n\nThe meal assistant uses a small recipe collection written for ShifaDaily and a food guide based on the leaflet you shared.

Last updated: 19 October 2026

What is stored: the medications you enter (name, dose, schedule, notes), your dose history and its change log, your pantry, food preferences and allergies, saved recipes and app settings.

Where: only in ShifaDaily's private storage on this phone. The app has no internet permission. It sends nothing to us or to anyone else, and has no account, analytics, advertising or crash-reporting service.

Backups: ShifaDaily's data is excluded from Android cloud backup and device-to-device transfer, so your health data does not leave the phone automatically. This also means it is not restored on a new phone. Use "Export my data" if you want a copy.

Export: an export is a readable file saved where you choose. You control who sees it.

Deletion: "Erase all data" in Settings deletes everything. Uninstalling the app also deletes its data.

Security: data is protected by Android's app sandbox and the phone's storage encryption. It is not additionally encrypted by ShifaDaily, so anyone who can unlock your phone, or a rooted or compromised phone, may be able to access it. Use a screen lock.

Notifications: reminder content is hidden on the lock screen by default and shows the full medication name only when the phone is unlocked (this depends on your phone's lock-screen settings).

Children: ShifaDaily is not designed for children.

Contact: see the support page on the official ShifaDaily website.
